decisions.reason: The equivalent embedding description allowed its branches to pass through further points of A cap B. The concentric-circle example separates it from the first clause, so this is a false equivalence in the definition.

F6 wrongly made every immersion an isometry onto its image, whereas the supplied definition requires a diffeomorphism. The actual map e in steps 4.1 and 5.1 is a proper embedding, so the proof has the stronger hypothesis needed and the result remains valid.

F4 stated the characteristic-two transfer short exact sequence for every covering although its two-lift argument requires exactly two sheets. Step 3.1 constructs a connected double cover, so the actual application meets that hypothesis.

F1 omitted closedness required by the ambient tubular-neighbourhood supplier. Its only application in step 1.1 is to the embedded boundary of compact N, which is compact and therefore closed in the Hausdorff target.

Clause (iv) confused a sufficient global hypothesis in Milnor Theorem 6.6 with a necessary condition for a selected clean disk. A local cancelling pair in a ball disjoint from a codimension-two sphere can have a clean disk although a complement meridian dies in the ambient fundamental group.

The general hypotheses had no orientations, but clause (iii) and step 2.2 invoked untwisted signed coefficients I(z) in Z[pi1(X)]. The supplied sign definition requires oriented ambient and sheet tangent spaces, so those coefficients were not defined in the stated generality.

F6 omitted closedness and step 4.1 applied its supplier directly to a disk with boundary and corners. That is outside the supplier interface, so the asserted oriented ambient neighbourhood had no licensed construction.

The Whitney-disk map definition allowed rank-zero interior patches while unconditionally asserting a rank-(m-2) normal bundle. Also, mere interior disjointness does not exclude tangency to a sheet along an open boundary edge, which would defeat the a-1 dimensional adapted-frame interface.

F5 falsely attributed radial complement transport to a Stiefel statement giving only nonemptiness, path connectivity and simple connectivity. Step 3.1 needed a global smooth normal frame before interpreting its boundary data as a Stiefel loop, so this strengthening supplied an essential unproved step.

F13 omitted the supplied relative Hurewicz theorem restriction n>=2 and its connectivity hypothesis. Step 2.1 is used only in the module cases p>=1 with fundamental groups identified, so n=p+1>=2 and the covered pair is (n-1)-connected with simply connected nonempty subspace.

reviews.reason: Added that both branches meet A cap B only at p,q and repaired the iff contract. The original arc clause already imposed exactly this condition; complementary transverse tangent spaces give the stated corner independence. Strict contract check: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Separated the immersion pullback criterion from the embedding isometry criterion in F6 and named the embedding hypothesis in step 5.1. Chartwise finite puncture avoidance, complete induced metric and minimizing-geodesic injectivity prove the stated arc; endpoint removal and the explicit constant-arc convention cover the remaining cases.

Restricted F4 to two-sheeted covers and clarified chain-basis injectivity. The meridian generates H1 of the disk complement by Mayer-Vietoris; transfer gives the upstairs meridian generator, killed by branched filling. Compact finite domination and universal coefficients then imply rational acyclicity. Statement unchanged.

Restored closedness in F1 and checked it explicitly for the embedded boundary before constructing the collar. Independent value/jet profiles avoid deficient ranks since m-n+1>n; separated-pair transversality has 2n-m<0 and local C1 injectivity handles near pairs. Relative protection and boundary collar homotopy remain valid; statement unchanged.

Corrected both occurrences to say complement pi1 injectivity is sufficient; the individual pushed-off loop, rather than every kernel element, is the actual obstruction. Added compatible orientation data for the signed group-ring language. Consulted the full Theorem 6.6 and proof through Lemma 6.13, printed pp.71-83, in the retrieved Milnor PDF. No Statement or Definition section exists, so this repair does not trigger interface propagation.

Preserved the orientation-free loop, arc-change and compatible-label criteria. Restricted only the signed coefficient comparison to oriented X,A,B with opposite signs, defined I(z)=epsilon(z)g(z), and explicitly oriented the torus witness by increasing x. The based cone filling and loop cancellation formulas give (i),(ii); compatible whiskers normalize g(p)=1 and g(q) to the circle class. Statement changed only in its signed clause; direct consumers are inventoried separately.

Removed the ambient tubular citation. Radial projection ODEs frame the disk-normal bundle; their determinant section extends in charts and patches by a smooth partition of unity, staying nonzero near the compact disk. Interval transport followed by Gram-Schmidt in the adapted metric gives smooth boundary frames; the opposite-sign calculation places endpoint frames in the same SO component. Updated only the owning contract entry; strict contract check passed after correcting trailing-tag extraction and inline-reference mappings: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Statement unchanged.

Retained general possibly singular Whitney disk maps, qualified the normal bundle to full-rank immersed and clean disks, and specified full two-dimensional immersion rank even at corners. Made sheet-adapted clean boundary collars explicit: tangent-plane intersection with each sheet is precisely the edge line. This is the collar data used in Milnor proof of Lemmas 6.7 and 6.13 and in all clean-disk suppliers. It permits the compatible-frame ranks without asserting a bundle for singular maps. Direct consumers require examination against the clarified normal and collar interfaces.

Restricted F5 to its actual interface. Added the proper Euclidean embedding prerequisite and proved radial projection transport directly using existing matrix-ODE and smooth-dependence suppliers: skew symmetry preserves U^TU and the commutator identity transports the projection. Gram-Schmidt uses the adapted metric. Stiefel simple connectivity now only fills the partial E frame; the transported complementary bundle supplies H, preserving orthogonality and sheet tangency. Part (i) retains its finite projection/Gram-Schmidt induction and choice-free sphere fillings. Owning contract and manifest entries reconciled under the shared lock; all focused checks passed.

Restated F13 with its exact range and connectivity assumptions and named n=p+1>=2 at the application. The finite relative cellular complex is exact below n; splitting surjections onto successive finitely generated projective bottom modules makes the nth cycle module finitely generated, without Noetherianity. Finite normal kernel generators handle p=1 before the module argument; determinant-compatible zero-surgery data handle p=0. Statement unchanged.
